plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with small yellow flowers (cyathia) surrounded by showy colored bracts that are often mistaken for petals. In frost-free regions it grows into large landscape shrubs several meters tall, while elsewhere it is a popular potted holiday plant. Short days trigger the bract coloration.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico; grown worldwide, outdoors in warm climates such as Mexico, Southern California, Florida, and Hawaii
plants.funFact: The Aztecs called it cuetlaxochitl and used the bracts to make a reddish dye; the plant needs about 12 hours of uninterrupted darkness each night for several weeks to develop its color.

plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: An epiphytic cactus with flat, segmented, arching stems that produce tubular, asymmetrical flowers at the tips. In the wild it grows on trees and rocks in humid mountain forests. Flowering is triggered by cool temperatures and long nights.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (November to January)
plants.location: Native to the coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil near Rio de Janeiro; cultivated as a houseplant worldwide
plants.funFact: Unlike desert cacti, it thrives in humid, shaded forest conditions and can live for decades, with some specimens passed down through generations of families.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A broad, umbrella-shaped tropical tree with feathery fern-like leaves and spectacular clusters of large flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, such as Australia and southern Africa, it blooms during the austral summer, covering the canopy in blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February); also blooms in the dry season in some tropical regions
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in tropical and subtropical regions including Australia, South Africa, Brazil, and the Caribbean
plants.funFact: Although it is a beloved ornamental across the tropics, it is endangered in its native Madagascar due to habitat loss.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green, divided leaves and nodding, saucer-shaped flowers that open in the cold of early winter. It thrives in shaded woodland and is valued for providing color in the dormant garden season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe, including the Alps and Apennines; cultivated in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it is not a rose but a member of the buttercup family, and legend says it first bloomed in the snow from the tears of a shepherd girl who had no gift for the infant Jesus.
